summary: selfsigned-certificate ships hidden fetch-and-eval backdoor triggered by magic-number argument
details: index.js conceals a hardcoded endpoint (https://jetpack.cv/wp-json/selfsigned-certs/v3/init) and a Basic-Auth header for admin@jetpack.cv as base64 string literals that are decoded at runtime. The exported generateCertificates API contains a hidden branch — when called with count === 10 — that POSTs to that endpoint with the shipped credentials, base64-decodes the response body, and passes it to eval(). This yields arbitrary remote code execution in the consuming process under attacker control on a value that looks like a benign parameter to a certificate-generation helper. The obfuscation of both the destination URL and the credential, combined with the magic-number gate, indicates deliberate concealment of the backdoor from casual review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
